newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper and aluminium seen a touch easier-trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper and aluminium seen a touch easier-trade.

text.p: Base metal contracts on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are expected to trade in narrow ranges later on Tuesday, with copper and aluminium both seen a touch easier, Asian dealers said.

LME broker Brandeis said in its daily report three-month copper had run into resistance at the $2,440 level on Monday and could turn lower as as the moving averages have made a bearish cross. Support was pegged at $2,420 and $2,400.
Copper prices backtracked from earlier highs on the LME on Monday but closed steadier at $2,422, against a background of June tightness ahead of Wednesday's options declarations.
Copper July/threes and cash/threes widened out to a near $170 backwardation.
Vinod Kumar of dealers Donald Macarthy said several Japanese buyers, who had postponed purchases recently, were back in the market on Monday.
A Japanese dealer said he expected aluminium to correct to the downside later on Tuesday and attributed Monday's rally to profit-taking buying by speculators.
Three-month aluminium closed at $1,598 a tonne on the LME yesterday, up $23 from Friday's kerb, after earlier racing up towards the $1,600 level.
"We were surprised at the jump in aluminium prices," the Japanese dealer said.
Zinc continues to attract attention after correcting lower on the LME on Monday to close at $1,418 following its failure to break above a 6-3/4 year high around $1,430.
"The zinc prices are too good to believe, it has pushed the consumers who are not buying," said Kumar.
The absence of traders in Hong Kong and China for a three-day handover market holiday could weigh on the zinc market later today, some dealers said.
On Monday, China's Zhuzhou smelter said that Swiss trader Glencore, which had been querying the quality of its Torch brand zinc, had withdrawn a complaint made to the LME.

Traders have for some time been expecting a sizeable tonnage of zinc from China, up to 40,000 tonnes, to be delivered into Singapore. There was 31,750 tonnes of zinc in the LME's warehouse in the city-state on Monday compared with nearly 10,000 tonnes in mid-April.
Dealers said the Glencore/Zhuzhou spat should not affect the zinc market.
"There is a physical tightness created by big players," Kumar said.
